newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weaker on foreign dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weaker on foreign dlr buying.

text.p: The Mexican peso lost ground gained from the dollar at the close of trade on Friday after zizagging through the session on swiftly changing and heavy deals, traders said.
"Many foreign brokers were trading hefty amounts; that's why rates moved around so much during the session," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour counterpart ended 1.8 and 2.65 percent weaker, respectively, at 7.9250/7.9290 and 7.9230/7.9275 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts earlier closed 1.5 centavos firmer at 7.8920/7.8970 per dollar.
Some traders said the peso had wavered in line with the changing fortunes of the U.S. stock and bond markets.

During late trade, the Dow Jones Industrial average was up 28.90 points at 7,165.12, after recovering from a low of 7,094.48. The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile up 15/32 to yield 6.90 percent.
